reference: There is no matching GNU DHCPv6 server CLI in this environment; the source status documentation records Kea as missing, so this suite has no parity cases. Contract expectations use Bash's documented type/help behavior and the public version/help strings. Deterministic DHCPv6 packet expectations were assembled independently from RFC 8415 message and option codes, lengths, fixed fixture values, and IPv6 encodings; the RECONFIGURE digest was computed independently with Python's standard-library hmac/hashlib implementation. No expected bytes were copied from candidate output.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata, including the documented public verbs and configuration keys
Exact deterministic offline SOLICIT-to-ADVERTISE and INFORMATION-REQUEST-to-REPLY packets
RELEASE reply encoding and removal limited to the matching client DUID and IAID in the lease file
Deterministic authenticated RECONFIGURE encoding with fixed transaction ID and replay value
Malformed packet hex rejection and absence of lease-file mutation
Offline RELAY-FORW/RELAY-REPL envelope, interface ID echo and output-variable binding without sockets.
exclusions: Live serve/run socket exchange is deferred because this task forbids network activity; the deferred case requires an isolated disposable network fixture and an independent DHCPv6 peer.
Live relay datagram transport remains part of the deferred server exchange; offline relay envelope processing is covered.
Successful leasequery lifetime fields are deferred until a frozen clock or clock mock and an independent RFC 5007 encoder are available.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify dhcpd6 as a builtin without relying on an external executable.
The Bash help summary must expose the documented DHCPv6 server description.
The full help text must advertise the documented server, host-testable seams, reconfigure operation, and configuration keys.
cases.script:
doc=$(help dhcpd6)
[[ $doc == *'dhcpd6 serve [-c CONFIG] [-l LEASEDB] [-i IFACE] [--once]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'dhcpd6 respond HEX [-c CONFIG] [-l LEASEDB] [-V VAR]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'dhcpd6 leasequery HEX [-c CONFIG] [-l LEASEDB] [-V VAR]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'dhcpd6 reconfigure --client-duid HEX --server-duid HEX --key HEX'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'Config keys: server-duid <hex>, pool-start <ipv6>, pool-size <n>,'* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'documented help sections present'

cases.purpose: The no-side-effect version option must print the public version contract exactly.

A fixed SOLICIT with CLIENTID and IA_NA must produce an RFC 8415 ADVERTISE with the first configured address, configured lifetimes, success status, and DNS option; an offer must leave the lease DB absent.
A fixed INFORMATION-REQUEST must receive a stateless REPLY carrying server/client IDs and the configured DNS server, with no lease DB created.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'server-duid 00030001020000000002' 'pool-start 2001:db8::10' 'pool-size 4' 'dns 2001:db8::53' 'lease-pref 300' 'lease-valid 600' 't1 120' 't2 480' > dhcp.conf
packet=0babcdef0001000a00030001020000000001
expected=07abcdef0002000a000300010200000000020001000a000300010200000000010017001020010db8000000000000000000000053
reply=$(dhcpd6 respond "$packet" -c dhcp.conf -l leases)
[[ $reply == "$expected" && ! -e leases ]]
printf '%s\n' "$reply"

cases.purpose: RELEASE must return a deterministic success REPLY and remove only the matching client's requested IAID while retaining its other IAID and another client's lease.
Fixed IDs, key, transaction ID, and replay value must produce the independently computed DHCPv6 RECONFIGURE HMAC-MD5 packet.
Malformed request hex must be rejected with usage status and a diagnostic before changing the lease DB.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'server-duid 00030001020000000002' 'pool-start 2001:db8::10' 'pool-size 4' > dhcp.conf
if dhcpd6 respond 0112zz -c dhcp.conf -l leases; then
  exit 1
else
  rc=$?
fi
[[ $rc -eq 2 && ! -e leases ]]
printf '%s\n' 'malformed hex rejected without lease mutation'
cases.stdout: malformed hex rejected without lease mutation

cases.purpose: Verify serve/run bind behavior and the full client-visible DHCPv6 exchange using an isolated peer, without treating offline seams as proof of socket behavior.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or isolated network mock with a controlled DHCPv6 client on UDP 546 and server endpoint on UDP 547, an independent RFC 8415 peer/oracle, packet capture, and lease-file checks. This suite's safety scope forbids network activity, so no live serve/run operation is executed or claimed passed.

cases.purpose: Offline RFC 8415 RELAY-FORW to RELAY-REPL encoding echoes hop/link/peer and interface ID around a stateless INFORMATION-REQUEST. Inputs/expected envelope are independently packed; no socket is opened.
Verify RFC 5007 queries by address and client ID, including active lease data, misses, and bounded preferred/valid remaining lifetime fields.
cases.reason: A meaningful success-path oracle needs a frozen clock or clock mock plus an independent RFC 5007 encoder to check IAADDR lifetimes and CLT_TIME across boundary values. No matching GNU/Kea reference is available, and this operation is not claimed passed; run it later with a disposable deterministic clock/reference fixture.

cases.purpose: Offline reply variable binding preserves the exact independent INFORMATION-REQUEST packet expectation.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'server-duid 00030001020000000002' 'pool-start 2001:db8::10' 'pool-size 4' 'dns 2001:db8::53' 'lease-pref 300' 'lease-valid 600' 't1 120' 't2 480' > dhcp.conf
dhcpd6 respond 0babcdef0001000a00030001020000000001 -c dhcp.conf -l leases -V reply
printf '%s\n' "$reply"
[[ ! -e leases ]]
